## Clinical Trials Now Enrolling

#### CALL FOR PATIENTS: Clinical Trial for Soft Tissue Sarcoma in Dogs

Study Title: Feasibility and dose-optimization clinical trial of local immunotherapy for solid tumors in canine cancer patients

Eligibility: Any dog weighing 5kg or above with at least one cutaneous soft tissue sarcoma lesion that is greater than 1.7cm in diameter is eligible to enroll. All dogs that meet the study criteria will receive the study drug (no placebo) followed by surgical removal of the tumor 1 week later.

Study Purpose: This clinical trial evaluates the safety, feasibility, and biological effects of a newly designed immunotherapy. Specifically, the study is evaluating the injection of investigational T-cell engagers (TCEs) directly into tumors (intratumorally) in canine patients with soft tissue sarcoma (STS). TCEs are engineered antibodies that physically connect T cells to cancer cells by targeting specific markers (CD3 or CD28 on T cells, and B7-H3 or PD-L1 on cancer cells), triggering the immune system to destroy tumor cells.

# Veterinary Clinical Trials

Clinical trials at VROC help evaluate new cancer treatments for pets by assessing their safety, effectiveness, and potential side effects. Participation is entirely voluntary, and the decision to enroll your pet is yours. However, enrollment in a clinical trial is required for a patient to be seen in our clinic.

Our studies build upon the current standard of care using the same advanced technologies available in leading specialty pet cancer hospitals. While specific outcomes cannot be guaranteed, our team is committed to providing the highest standard of veterinary oncology care throughout each trial.

For questions or to learn more about available studies, please contact Paige Neumann, Research Study Coordinator, at 214-645-6221 or by VROC@UTSouthwestern.edu (no-reply@utsouthwestern.edu).

# Advancing Canine Brain Tumor Treatment

Image: A black and white Boston Terrier on an exam table

## What We Do

The Canine Brain Tumor Program provides advanced clinical care for dogs while accelerating human brain tumor research.

## About the program

The University of Minnesota Canine Brain Tumor Program is a multifaceted, internationally recognized program that advances care for both dogs and people affected by primary brain tumors. We provide cutting-edge therapy to dogs to preserve their quality of life and improve long-term survival. We study how canine and human gliomas are similar to each other, so that the clinical trials we conduct benefit both dogs and people. Our trials are supported by a variety of financial sponsors, including grants from foundations and government agencies. The majority of costs associated with enrollment are covered through these funding mechanisms.

## Join our clinical trials

Enroll now

## Collaborate with us

The CBTP partners with scientific organizations conducting cutting edge clinical research. Our goal is to unite canine brain tumor patients with innovative diagnostic and treatment options. To learn more about collaborating with the CBTP, please contact us at [email protected].

See all current clinical trials in the Clinical Investigation Center.

Research ethics at the University of Minnesota. We are committed to protecting research participants, upholding ethical standards, and improving our practice at every step of our work.

# SBRT for Canine Lung Tumor Study

  * Recruiting
  * Dog
  * Oncology

Primary pulmonary carcinomas in dogs are most commonly treated with surgery, which can result in survival times of approximately one year. Stereotactic body radiation therapy (SBRT) is a highly precise form of radiation therapy that delivers high doses of radiation directly to a tumor while minimizing exposure to surrounding normal tissues. The purpose of this study is to evaluate dogs with primary pulmonary carcinoma treated using a standardized SBRT protocol across institutions participating in the Veterinary Radiation Therapy Oncology Group (VRTOG).

## Inclusion Criteria

Dogs are eligible for enrollment if they meet all of the following criteria:

  * Cytologic or histopathologic diagnosis of a single primary pulmonary carcinoma.
  * Primary lung tumor measuring greater than 1 cm in its shortest diameter.
  * No previous treatment for the lung tumor.
  * No diagnosis of another malignant tumor outside the lungs within 30 days before enrollment.

# COOL - Clinical Trials

At the Comparative Oral Oncology Laboratory (COOL), our research bridges discovery and clinical patient care. Through targeted clinical trials, we offer novel diagnostic and therapeutic strategies for companion animals facing oral cancers.

## Active Trial: Novel Targeted Oral Therapy for Canine Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma (OSCC)

Squamous Cell Carcinoma is the second most common oral malignancy in dogs. Because these tumors are locally invasive, rapidly erode bone, and frequently recur following conventional treatments, surgical options are sometimes limited.

This study evaluates Trametinib, an FDA-approved targeted oral medication used in human oncology. Having established its safety in dogs, our goal in this expanded trial is to identify specific molecular and genetic profiles that predict favorable treatment response, allowing us to deliver precise, effective targeted therapy.

Eligibility: Dogs presented to or evaluated through the Cornell University Hospital for Animals (CUHA) with a biopsy-confirmed or strongly suspected oral squamous cell carcinoma.

Financial Coverage: All diagnostic imaging, physical exams, sedation, follow-up procedures, and trial medications required during the study are provided free of charge. Additionally, dogs that complete the 126-day protocol receive an additional $1,000 credit toward standard-of-care follow-up therapy.

Owner Commitment: Administer oral medication once daily at home (chemotherapy handling and safety guidance provided).

Bring your dog to CUHA for scheduled re-checks on or around Days 14, 42, 70, 108, and 126.

Complete short weekly health status surveys (via phone or in-person during visits).

Final Evaluation (Day 126): Includes a physical exam, full-body CT scan under general anesthesia to document treatment response, tumor biopsy, and fine-needle aspirates of mandibular lymph nodes for genomic analysis.

Study Leadership: Santiago Peralta, DVM, Dipl. AVDC, Founding Fellow AVDC-OMFS

Sponsor: Funded by the Cornell Richard P. Riney Canine Health Center.

How to Enroll or Refer a Patient: If you are a dog owner interested in screening, or a veterinarian seeking to refer a patient for trial evaluation:

Phone: (607) 253-3060 (Request the Dentistry & Oral Surgery or Oncology Service)

Email: vet-research@cornell.edu

Location: Cornell University Hospital for Animals, Ithaca, NY

## 犬の組織球性肉腫に対する抗PD-1抗体を用いた臨床試験

犬の組織球性肉腫は極めて悪性の癌であり、急速に進行することが知られていますが有効な治療法は確立されていません。
近年、人においてPD-1という分子を標的とした抗体薬を用いた免疫療法が、がん患者の一部で有効であることがわかってきました。また犬においても山口大学のこれまでの臨床試験によりある種のがんに対して効果があることが明らかとなりました。
そこで、あらたに犬の組織球肉腫に対する犬PD-1に対する抗体薬の有効性と安全性を調べるために、臨床試験を実施しています。なお、この試験は2026年7月に当センター臨床試験委員会において倫理的承認を受けております。

### 対象(抜粋)

  * 当センターでの生検から組織球性肉腫と診断されること
  * 生検後も各種検査で病変が検出されること
  * 免疫抑制剤投与や免疫療法を受けていないこと
  * 当センターへの定期的な通院が可能であること

※このほかにも複数の基準があります。特に、大型犬の場合は必ずしも参加できない可能性があることをご了承ください。

### 内容 (抜粋)

  * 当センターにて組織生検による確定診断を実施します。
  * 臨床試験内容の詳細を説明し、参加の意思を確認します。
  * 参加していただく場合は試験薬を2週間に一回静脈内投与し、その効果と副作用を当院にて確認します。

ご協力いただける方は下記連絡先(当センター受付)までご連絡ください。

## Study title

Engaging the Immune System to Kill Solid Tumors in Pet Dogs - A Comparative Oncology Approach (TriKE + Radiation Therapy)

## Purpose of study

The purpose of the study is to identify a safe and effective dose of a novel immunotherapy drug (TriKE) when given with hypofractionated radiation therapy (RT) in companion dogs with a sarcoma. 

## Eligibility criteria

Dogs must: 

  * Have cytologically or histopathologicaly confirmed sarcoma, measuring at least 2cm
  * Weigh at least 7 kg (15 lbs)
  * Modified performance score less than 2 and expected survival of at least 2 months

# Canine Cancer Clinical Trials

# Canine cancer clinical trials at the University of Minnesota

## Modiano Lab clinical trials

Modiano lab clinical trials are facilitated by the College of Veterinary Medicine's Clinical Investigation Center (CIC). The CIC is the central location for veterinary clinical trials and translational research studies for faculty at the College. Learn more about the CIC on their website

Explore the current Modiano Lab clinical trials. 

COED Part 1: Sample collection: Dogs with cancer and healthy dogs aged 2-4

COED Part 2: Early detection of canine osteosarcoma

LyRA 1: Blood collection study for lymphoma 

LyRA 3: Blood collection study for lymphoma in healthy dogs at least 5 years old

ORBIT: VSV and anti-PD-1 inhibitor for Canine B-cell Lymphoma

### Other clinical trials

Visit the University of Minnesota’s Clinical Investigation Center, for current enrollment information for all pet animal clinical trials.

### About clinical trials

Clinical trials, or clinical studies, take place in the clinic, a step after lab research studies. They offer experimental treatments to patients who fit the criteria of a particular study and are used to determine whether new drugs or treatments are both safe and effective.

There is some risk with any clinical trial, just as with many medical procedures; however, all clinical trials are reviewed by an Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC) before they can begin. Also, informed owner consent is always part of clinical trials, so before your pet enters a study you will be given all information up front and must agree in writing. In many clinical trials, patients must be treated at the clinic conducting the trial and may not receive study drugs remotely.

Research ethics at the University of Minnesota. We are committed to protecting research participants, upholding ethical standards, and improving our practice at every step of our work.
